about: State-controlled operator of nine South African airports, including OR Tambo International in Johannesburg, Cape Town International and King Shaka International in Durban, handling tens of millions of passengers a year. Based in Bedfordview near Johannesburg, ACSA is majority owned by the South African government with the Public Investment Corporation as a minority shareholder. Revenue comes from airport charges, retail, parking and property. Customers are airlines, passengers and retail tenants. High public visibility in South Africa as an infrastructure operator.

Canadian aviation company in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia, with two main businesses: regional airline capacity flown for Air Canada as Jazz, and aircraft leasing, including regional jets and turboprops, plus a spare parts and maintenance unit. Customers are Air Canada and other airlines. Revenue comes from fixed-fee flying contracts and leases. Listed on the TSX (CHR). Passengers know Jazz and Air Canada Express flights, while Chorus itself is a B2B name.

National airline of Kenya, flying from Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi to dozens of destinations across Africa, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, with a fleet of around 40 aircraft. A member of the SkyTeam alliance and listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange, it is partly owned by the Kenyan government and creditors after a 2019 restructuring. Founded in 1977. Strong national brand and a visible sponsor in African sport.

Aircraft lessors are B2B businesses selling to airlines, oil and gas support operators and emergency medical services, with no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Cruise company operating Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea, plus a stake in TUI Cruises, with more than 65 ships and private destinations such as Perfect Day at CocoCay. Sells cruise vacations to consumers through travel agents and direct bookings, with revenue near 16 billion dollars. Headquartered in Miami, Florida; founded 1968. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RCL). Strong consumer brands in the US and Europe, with a history of sports sponsorship and marketing partnerships.

Online marketplace for short-term home rentals and experiences, connecting hosts with travellers in more than 220 countries and regions, with millions of listings. Earns service fees from guests and hosts, with revenue around 12 billion dollars and over 4 billion guest arrivals since founding. Headquartered in San Francisco; founded 2008. Listed on Nasdaq (ABNB) since its 2020 IPO. Globally recognised consumer brand, and a past Olympic and Paralympic sponsor and partner of major sports and events.

British luxury sports car manufacturer producing the DB12, Vantage, DBX SUV, Valhalla and Valkyrie, sold to wealthy collectors through dealers. Makes cars at Gaydon and St Athan, with sales of around 6,000 units and revenue near 1.5 billion pounds, typically loss-making. Headquartered in Gaydon, Warwickshire; founded 1913. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (AML), with Lawrence Stroll's consortium and Saudi PIF as large shareholders. Iconic consumer brand and a Formula 1 works team (Aston Martin Aramco) since 2021.

Global travel retail and food service group, created by the 2023 merger of Dufry and Autogrill, operating duty-free and convenience shops (Dufry, Hudson, Duty Free) and restaurants in airports, railway stations, motorway services and cruise ships in 70 countries. Revenue near 14 billion Swiss francs from travelling consumers. Headquartered in Basel. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (AVOL). Visible to travellers as airport retail brands, with limited stand-alone brand awareness.

Online travel group operating Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Travelocity, Wotif and the B2B Expedia Partner Solutions, selling flights, hotels, vacation rentals and packages to travellers worldwide. Earns commissions and advertising, with gross bookings above 100 billion dollars and revenue near 13 billion dollars. Headquartered in Seattle, Washington; spun out of Microsoft in 1996. Listed on Nasdaq (EXPE), with Liberty Expedia and Barry Diller's family as major shareholders. Widely known consumer travel brands with marketing and sports partnerships.

Car rental company operating Hertz, Dollar and Thrifty brands at airports and city locations in North America, Europe and elsewhere, and renting to leisure and business travellers plus Firefly, and it has used EVs including Tesla in its fleet. Revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Estero, Florida; founded 1918. Listed on Nasdaq (HTZ), emerged from 2021 bankruptcy with Knighthead and Certares as large holders. Major consumer travel brand with a long motorsport and sports marketing record.

Timeshare and vacation ownership company selling points-based membership at resorts under Hilton Grand Vacations, Diamond Resorts and Bluegreen, operating more than 150 properties in the US, Europe, Asia and the Caribbean, with about 700,000 owner families. Earns from sales, financing and management fees, with revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Orlando, Florida; spun off from Hilton in 2017. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HGV). Consumer brand tied to Hilton.

Cruise operator, part of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings that also owns Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises. NCL runs around 20 ships with 'Freestyle Cruising' and sells cruise vacations to consumers via travel advisers and online, and a private island Great Stirrup Cay. The group has revenue near 9.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Miami, Florida; founded 1966. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NCLH). Well-known cruise brand in the US and Europe, with some sports sponsorship.

US lodging real estate investment trust owning about 40 upscale and luxury hotels in leading urban and resort markets, including Hilton Hawaiian Village, Hilton Chicago and Casa Marina, mostly operated by Hilton, Hyatt and Marriott brands. Earns room and hospitality revenue, with over 2.5 billion dollars annual revenue. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia; spun off from Hilton in 2017. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (PK). Property owner, not a consumer brand, with guests booking under Hilton or Hyatt names.

US real estate investment trust owning large convention and entertainment hotels operated by Marriott, such as Gaylord Opryland in Nashville, Gaylord Texan, Gaylord Palms, Gaylord National, plus the Grand Ole Opry and the Ole Red venues. Earns hospitality revenue from group business and entertainment, near 2.3 billion dollars. Headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RHP). Strong destination brands in Nashville, though a niche brand to wider consumers.

Travel and Leisure Co. is a timeshare and travel club company running the Wyndham Destinations vacation ownership business, Club Wyndham, WorldMark and the Travel + Leisure membership and magazine brand, plus Panorama exchange via RCI. Customers are vacation owners and members, with revenue near 4 billion dollars. Headquartered in Orlando, Florida; spun out of Wyndham in 2018. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TNL). Consumer travel brand known through the Travel + Leisure name.

Luxury integrated resort and casino operator running Wynn Las Vegas and Encore in Nevada, Wynn Macau and Wynn Palace in Macau, plus a new Wynn Al Marjan Island resort being built in the UAE (Ras Al Khaimah). Customers are high-end gamblers, leisure guests and event attendees, with revenue near 7 billion dollars. Headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada; founded by Steve Wynn in 2002. Listed on Nasdaq (WYNN). Strong luxury casino brand globally and a partner in Formula 1 Las Vegas events.

World's largest cruise company, operating Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, P&O Cruises, Cunard, Costa Cruises and AIDA with around 90 ships. Sells cruise holidays to millions of consumers a year, with revenue near 25 billion dollars. Headquartered in Miami, Florida, with Carnival plc in the UK; founded 1972. Dual listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CCL) and London (CCL). Very strong consumer brands with sports and entertainment sponsorships.

Indian hospitality technology company that signs up independent hotels and homes into a branded network (OYO Rooms, OYO Townhouse, Belvilla in Europe, and Oravel Stays), operating mainly in India, Southeast Asia, Europe and the US. Earns commissions and revenue share from hotels, with a large chain presence. Headquartered in Gurugram; founded 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal. Private (parent PRISM) backed by SoftBank, which cut its valuation sharply; a listing was planned. Widely recognised budget hotel brand in India.

Allegiant Travel Company is a US ultra-low-cost airline group flying leisure travellers from smaller cities to vacation destinations in Florida, Las Vegas and elsewhere, selling flights alongside hotels and attractions. Operates Allegiant Air, with revenue near 2.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada; founded 1997. Listed on Nasdaq (ALGT). Recognised leisure airline brand in the US, with naming rights at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas.

Marriott Vacations Worldwide is a US timeshare and vacation ownership company that sells and manages vacation club points under Marriott Vacation Club, Westin, Sheraton, Hyatt and Interval International. Customers are vacation owners and members, with revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Orlando, Florida; spun off from Marriott International in 2011. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (VAC). Consumer brands are licensed from Marriott.

Wyndham Hotels & Resorts is the world's largest hotel franchisor by number of properties, with about 9,000 hotels in around 95 countries under brands such as Wyndham, Days Inn, Super 8, Ramada, La Quinta, Microtel, Baymont and Howard Johnson. Earns franchise fees. Headquartered in Parsippany, New Jersey; spun off from Wyndham Worldwide in 2018. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (WH). Familiar budget brands to travellers in the US.

Booking Holdings is the world's largest online travel company, headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut. Its brands include Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, offering hotel and flight reservations, car rentals and restaurant bookings, earning commissions and advertising fees. Revenue is above $23bn with about 24,000 employees, serving travellers in 200+ countries. Listed on Nasdaq (BKNG). Booking.com is a major consumer brand with huge advertising spend, and the group has used sports sponsorship, including Booking.com's tie-ups in football and with Formula 1 rival series.

MGM Resorts International is a Las Vegas hospitality and gaming company operating casino resorts including Bellagio, MGM Grand, ARIA, Cosmopolitan, Mandalay Bay and Luxor in Las Vegas, plus resorts in Macau and regional US markets, and the online sports betting and gaming business BetMGM, a joint venture with Entain. It earns from gaming, rooms, dining, entertainment and conventions, with annual revenue about $17bn. Listed on the NYSE (MGM). Very strong consumer brand and a prolific sports sponsor, with an official F1 partnership via MGM and Las Vegas Grand Prix ties.

Sandals Resorts International is a luxury all-inclusive resort operator headquartered in Montego Bay, Jamaica, and founded by Gordon Butch Stewart in 1981. It runs Sandals (couples-focused) and Beaches (family-focused) resorts across the Caribbean in Jamaica, Saint Lucia, Antigua, Barbados, Grenada, the Bahamas and elsewhere. Guests are mostly North American and UK vacationers, with revenue from room rates, packages and add-ons. Privately owned by the Stewart family, now run by Adam Stewart. Strong consumer brand recognition in the US and UK through heavy advertising.

Another Star is based in Leiden, the Netherlands, and is described by Crunchbase as a hotel chain that operates hotels and related hospitality and leisure businesses. The input lists hospitality, hotel and leisure as its industries and shows funding of about $2.0bn, with the latest round in November 2025. The business model is likely accommodation revenue, but the input gives no further detail on brands, size or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Brex is a San Francisco fintech providing corporate cards, spend management, expense software, travel and banking tools for start-ups and large businesses. Customers range from early-stage tech firms to large enterprises, and it earns interchange fees, software subscriptions and interest. Founded in 2017 by Henrique Dubugras and Pedro Franceschi, it raised over $1.6bn and was valued at about $12bn in 2022. Private. B2B brand known in tech and start-up circles.

Hyatt Hotels Corporation is a Chicago-based global hospitality company with more than 1,400 hotels and all-inclusive resorts in about 80 countries. Brands include Park Hyatt, Grand Hyatt, Hyatt Regency, Andaz, Alila, Hyatt Place and Hyatt House, and the Hyatt Inclusive Collection. It earns fees from managed and franchised properties, plus owned hotels, with the World of Hyatt loyalty programme. Revenue is around $6.5bn. Listed on the NYSE (H), controlled by the Pritzker family trusts. Strong consumer brand, particularly among business and premium travellers.

Red Sea Global is a Saudi Arabian developer of luxury regenerative tourism destinations on the Red Sea coast, owned by the Public Investment Fund and based in Riyadh. Projects include The Red Sea (a set of islands and resorts with Six Senses, Ritz-Carlton and others, opened 2023) and Amaala, plus a private airport, utilities and the Red Sea International Airport. It earns from hotel, real estate and operating revenue and is state-backed. Government-owned. It is a growing sports-sponsorship name, with deals in football and sailing.

Abercrombie and Kent is a global luxury travel company, founded in 1962 by Geoffrey Kent in Kenya, offering private journeys, safaris, cruises and small-group tours in over 100 countries, with offices worldwide and a US base in Downers Grove, Illinois. Customers are affluent leisure travellers, earning revenue from tour and trip bookings. Privately held, with investors including Dubai-based and US capital. A premium travel brand with strong awareness among high-net-worth travellers.

American Express Global Business Travel (Amex GBT) is a New York corporate travel management company providing booking tools, expense management and meetings services to businesses, with acquisition of CWT in 2025. It serves thousands of corporate clients in over 140 countries and earns transaction fees. Listed on the NYSE (GBTG) since a 2022 SPAC, with American Express, Qatar Investment Authority and Juweel as major holders. B2B, well known to travel buyers, with the Amex-linked brand partly visible.

Summit Hotel Properties is a hotel real estate investment trust, based in Austin, Texas with an input address elsewhere in California, owning upscale select-service hotels under Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt brands such as Courtyard, Hampton Inn and Hyatt Place in the US. Revenue comes from hotel operations. Listed on the NYSE (INN). Property owner; guests see the franchise brands rather than Summit, so consumer awareness is low.

Transat A.T. is a Montreal-based integrated Canadian tour operator and airline group, selling vacation packages, flights and hotel stays to destinations in the Caribbean, Europe and Mexico under Air Transat and the Transat travel brand, with offices in Canada, France and the UK. Revenue is about C$2.9bn. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TRZ). Strong Canadian consumer travel brand, with Air Transat well known in Quebec and across Canada.

Travelport is a global travel technology company, based in Langley, Berkshire, whose distribution platform connects airlines, hotels and car rental firms to travel agencies and online booking sites. It earns transaction fees from bookings, and in 2019 was taken private by Siris Capital and Elliott. The company later combined with others and carries a sizeable debt load. Private. B2B travel platform, with no consumer brand awareness.

A&O Hotels and Hostels is a Berlin-based budget hotel and hostel chain with around 40 locations in Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, the Czech Republic, Italy, Denmark, Hungary and the UK, offering private rooms and dorm beds to young travellers, families and school groups. Founded in 2000, it earns room revenue from accommodation and is privately held with private equity backing. Reasonably known in Germany among budget travellers, with little profile elsewhere.

about: Battersea Power Station is a London regeneration site on the Thames, a former coal-fired power station redeveloped into a mixed-use district with apartments, offices (Apple's UK headquarters), shops, restaurants, leisure venues and an events venue, with a Northern line station. It is owned by a Malaysian consortium of Sime Darby Property, SP Setia and the Employees Provident Fund. The input lists a funding amount of GBP 880m. Visitor-oriented property venue, with significant London consumer awareness.

Las Vegas Sands is a Las Vegas-based resort developer and operator of integrated casino resorts. It sold its Las Vegas properties, the Venetian and Palazzo, in 2022 and now focuses on Singapore (Marina Bay Sands) and Macau (The Venetian Macao, The Londoner, The Parisian). Revenue is around $11bn, earned from gaming, hotel, retail, convention and entertainment. Listed on the NYSE (LVS), controlled by the Adelson family. Marina Bay Sands is an iconic Singapore landmark with strong travel brand visibility.

Melia Hotels International is a Palma de Mallorca-based Spanish hotel group, one of the largest holiday hotel operators in the world, running around 400 hotels in about 40 countries under Melia, Gran Melia, ME, Paradisus, Innside and Sol brands, strong in Spain, the Caribbean and Latin America. Revenue is about EUR 2bn. Listed on the Spanish stock exchange (MEL), with the Escarrer family in control. Strong consumer brand in Spanish-speaking markets and a sponsor of sports.

Melco Resorts and Entertainment is a Hong Kong-based casino resort developer and operator with properties in Macau (City of Dreams, Studio City, Altira), Manila (City of Dreams Manila) and Cyprus. Led by Lawrence Ho, it earns from gaming, rooms, dining, entertainment and retail, with revenue near US$4.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (MLCO) and Hong Kong (6883). Strong consumer brand in Asian gaming and tourism, and a notable sponsor with a Macau Grand Prix link.

Tripadvisor is a Needham, Massachusetts travel platform where users read reviews and book hotels, tours, restaurants (via TheFork) and experiences, with brands including Viator, TheFork and Tripadvisor itself. It earns commissions and advertising and has revenue of about $1.8bn. Listed on Nasdaq (TRIP), with Liberty TripAdvisor merged in 2025. Very high consumer awareness in travel, with a community of reviewers and advertising partnerships.

Ashford Hospitality Trust is a Dallas, Texas hotel REIT that owns upscale and upper-midscale hotels across the US, mainly under Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt brands, advised by Ashford Inc. It earns revenue from hotel operations and has been highly leveraged, with a shrinking portfolio. Listed on the NYSE (AHT). Property owner, guests see the franchise brand rather than Ashford, so consumer awareness is low.

Fosun Tourism Group is a Shanghai-based Chinese resort and travel group owned by Fosun International, operating Club Med (acquired 2015), Atlantis Sanya, Thomas Cook brand assets in some markets and Foliday and Lijiang resorts. It earns room, tour and resort revenue. It listed in Hong Kong in 2018 (1992) and was later delisted from the Hong Kong market after Fosun's takeover. Club Med is a notable global leisure brand, popular in Europe and Asia.

Klook is a Singapore-based travel and leisure booking platform where users book attractions, tours, transport and activities, with a focus on Asia-Pacific travellers and destinations worldwide. It operates in over 2,500 destinations, with tens of millions of users and revenue of several hundred million dollars. Funding of about $1bn includes SoftBank, Sequoia, and Goldman Sachs. Private, preparing an IPO. Strong awareness among travellers in Asia, with partnerships in sports and travel.

Vail Resorts is a Broomfield, Colorado operator of about 40 mountain resorts, including Vail, Whistler Blackcomb, Park City, Breckenridge, Heavenly and Perisher, plus lodging and retail. It earns lift ticket, Epic Pass, ski school and dining revenue from skiers across North America, Europe and Australia, with revenue near $2.9bn. Listed on the NYSE (MTN). Strong brand among snow sports enthusiasts, and a notable sports and events promoter.

Welcome Break is a UK motorway service area operator, based in Newport Pagnell, Buckinghamshire, running about 40 sites with fuel stations, Starbucks, KFC, Burger King, M&S Food and Greggs outlets, plus Days Inn hotels. Roughly 50 million visitors a year pass through. Owned by the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, after Starwood's earlier ownership. Private. Familiar to UK drivers, with a retail-led brand, and potential for hospitality tie-ins.

Viking Cruises is a Basel, Switzerland-based cruise line founded by Torstein Hagen in 1997, operating river and ocean cruises and expedition ships to Europe, Asia, Egypt and the Americas under Viking River, Viking Ocean and Viking Expeditions. It targets affluent older travellers, sells directly, and has fleets of over 90 ships. It listed on the NYSE in 2024 (VIK). Strong brand recognition in the US and UK, known for sponsoring Masterpiece Theatre on PBS.

Asset World Corp is a Bangkok-based Thai hospitality and commercial property company, part of the TCC Group of billionaire Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi. It owns and operates hotels, convention centers, retail and mixed-use developments such as Asiatique, and office buildings in Thailand and overseas. Listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (AWC). Customers are travellers, event organisers, shoppers and tenants. Hotel and retail brands are known in Thailand, a mix of consumer and B2B exposure.
cb_desc: Asset World Corp is a member of TCC Group.

about: Scandic Hotels Group is the largest hotel operator in the Nordic region, based in Stockholm, with about 280 hotels in Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and Germany, and around 60,000 rooms. It earns revenue from room, restaurant and meeting income, mostly leased and managed properties. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (SHOT). Customers are business and leisure travellers. High consumer brand awareness in the Nordics, with a loyalty programme of millions of members.

Clara is a Brazilian corporate card and spend management fintech (a Mexico-founded startup, founded in 2021 by Gerry Giacomán and Diego Pérez, now with operations in Brazil, Colombia and Mexico). It offers corporate cards, expense management and payments to businesses. The input shows about $733 million in total funding, largely debt. B2B fintech with limited consumer awareness.

about: Cowarobot is a Chinese robotics company that develops AI-powered personal mobility products, such as self-driving suitcases and the Cowarobot R1 robotic scooter, and works on future travel experiences. Based in Shanghai, with a reported funding of about $871 million. Customers are consumers and corporate partners. Limited brand awareness outside Chinese tech circles.

about: Massachusetts Port Authority (Massport) is a Boston-based Massachusetts public authority that owns and operates Boston Logan International Airport, Hanscom Field, Worcester Regional Airport and the Port of Boston's seaport facilities and Conley Terminal. It earns revenue from airline fees, parking, concessions and property, and issues bonds, which explains its $780 million reported funding. Government-owned. Logan handles over 40 million passengers annually. High local visibility as an airport operator.

H World Group (formerly Huazhu Group, formerly China Lodging Group) is a Shanghai-based hotel operator with brands such as HanTing, Ji Hotel, Orange, JI, Crystal Orange, Steigenberger and Blossom House, with over 10,000 hotels in China and Europe, mostly franchised. Founded 2005 and listed on the Nasdaq and Hong Kong (HTHT, 1179). Customers are travellers and franchisees. Strong consumer brand awareness in China.

Pebblebrook Hotel Trust is a Bethesda, Maryland-based real estate investment trust (NYSE: PEB) that owns upscale and luxury lifestyle hotels in major US urban and resort destinations, including San Francisco, Los Angeles, Boston and Washington. Hotels are operated under third-party brands such as Marriott and Hyatt. Revenue is about $1.4 billion. Customers are travellers and meeting planners. Financial and property vehicle with little brand awareness itself.

Royal Caribbean Cruises is a Miami-based cruise operator, listed on NYSE (RCL), running Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea, with about 65 ships and the world's largest cruise ships (Icon of the Seas). Revenue is around $16 billion with over 6 million guests a year. It sells holidays to consumers worldwide, with its private island Perfect Day at CocoCay. Very high consumer brand awareness, partnering with sports and entertainment properties.

Six Flags is a US regional theme park operator based in Arlington, Texas, formed by the 2024 merger of Cedar Fair and Six Flags Entertainment, with about 40 amusement and water parks in the US, Canada and Mexico, including Cedar Point, Knott's Berry Farm and Magic Mountain. It earns revenue from admissions, season passes and in-park spending, with about 50 million visits a year. Listed on NYSE (FUN). Strong consumer brand in North America.

Wynn Macau is a luxury hotel and casino resort operator in Macau, a subsidiary of Wynn Resorts (Las Vegas), operating Wynn Macau and Wynn Palace resorts with luxury hotels, gaming, retail and dining. Listed on the Hong Kong exchange (1128). Customers are VIP and mass-market gamblers and tourists mostly from China. Strong luxury brand in Asia; gambling limits sponsorship fit in many markets.

Virgin Voyages is an adults-only cruise line based in Plantation, Florida, launched in 2020 with ships such as Scarlet Lady, Valiant Lady, Resilient Lady and Brilliant Lady, sailing from Miami and Mediterranean ports. Owned by Virgin Group and Bain Capital, it sells cruise holidays to consumers and groups with a focus on dining, wellness and entertainment. Founded 2014. Strong, lifestyle-led consumer brand with celebrity and creative marketing.

Trip.com Group is a leading online travel company headquartered in Shanghai and listed on Nasdaq (TCOM) and Hong Kong. Brands include Ctrip, Trip.com, Skyscanner and Qunar, offering flights, hotels, rail, packages and corporate travel to hundreds of millions of customers, mostly in China but expanding internationally. Founded 1999. Annual revenue is over 50 billion yuan. Strong consumer brand in Asia and, through Skyscanner, in Europe.

Four Seasons Private Residences Las Vegas is a branded residential development in the Las Vegas area of Nevada, associated with the Four Seasons hospitality brand, offering luxury private residences. The Crunchbase profile lists the company as a hospitality and real estate offering based in Henderson, Nevada. Developer, ownership and scale are not confirmed from the input. Luxury property with limited standalone brand awareness beyond the Four Seasons name. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Sonder was a San Francisco-based hospitality company offering serviced apartments and boutique hotel rooms booked through an app, operating thousands of units in North America, Europe and the Middle East. It listed on Nasdaq via a SPAC in 2022, signed a Marriott partnership in 2025, and then ran into severe financial difficulty and moved toward liquidation in late 2025. Founded 2014. Now likely defunct, so not an active sponsorship prospect.

about: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts is a Toronto-headquartered luxury hotel operator, founded in 1960 by Isadore Sharp, managing over 120 hotels, resorts and branded residences in more than 45 countries, including properties in Paris, New York, Maldives and Dubai. It earns management and licensing fees, and is owned by Cascade Investment (Bill Gates), Kingdom Holding (Prince Alwaleed) and Isadore Sharp. Customers are high-net-worth travellers. Premium global hospitality brand with long record in luxury partnerships.

Host Hotels & Resorts is the largest US lodging real estate investment trust, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland and listed on the NYSE (HST). It owns about 80 upscale and luxury hotels, with brands such as Ritz-Carlton, Four Seasons, Westin, Marriott and Hyatt operating them, in US cities and resort markets, with revenue near 5.5 billion dollars. Customers are hotel operators; the properties serve travellers. B2B real estate owner with low consumer visibility.

Athens International Airport, officially Eleftherios Venizelos, is Greece's main airport, located at Spata near Athens. It handles roughly 28 to 30 million passengers a year, serving airlines, passengers, retailers and advertisers. Revenue comes from airport charges, retail and property concessions, and advertising. It opened in 2001 and operates under a concession with Greek state shareholding alongside private investors. The airport brand is well known to travellers to Greece, and it offers advertising and partnership inventory. Crunchbase lists $500 million in funding, latest in June 2026.

Catalonia Hotels & Resorts is a family-owned Spanish hotel chain founded in 1983 in Barcelona, operating around 60 or more hotels in Spain, Portugal, the Caribbean (Dominican Republic and Mexico) and Latin America. Brands include Catalonia, Zentral Hotels and Royal Hideaway. Customers are leisure and business travellers, with income from hotel rooms and services. Private and not listed. Known regionally in the Spanish and Caribbean markets, moderate consumer awareness.

ITC Hotels is the hospitality arm of ITC Limited, running luxury and premium hotels under the ITC Hotels, Welcomhotel, Storii and Fortune brands, with about 140 hotels across India. Customers are business and leisure travellers, and revenue comes from rooms, food and beverage, and events. Headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana, it was demerged from ITC Ltd and listed on the NSE and BSE in January 2025. ITC remains a major shareholder. Strong luxury brand in India with notable restaurant brands such as Bukhara.

Swiss-headquartered luxury hotel and resort group, founded in 1988 by Adrian Zecha, operating Aman resorts and residences (such as Amanpuri, Amangiri and Aman Tokyo) in around 20 countries. Customers are very wealthy leisure travellers. Controlled by Vladislav Doronin's Aman Group. Small portfolio but an extremely strong luxury brand. The group manages a small number of resorts and its Aman New York hotel and branded residences are examples.

Berlin-based online marketplace founded in 2009 for booking tours, activities and attraction tickets in thousands of destinations, earning commission from suppliers on bookings by travellers worldwide. Raised around $1.1 billion and was valued at about $2 billion. Privately held. Well-known travel consumer brand in Europe and North America, with growing marketing activity. The company has hundreds of employees across Berlin and other cities, and works with tour operators and museums.

Norwegian coastal cruise and ferry operator, founded 2018, running the Hurtigruten route along Norway with four hybrid ships. Customers are leisure passengers and cargo shippers. Based in Fosnavag. Privately held, with regional visibility. Operates from Norwegian ports on the coastal route between Bergen and Kirkenes, carrying passengers and cargo. Brand has seasonal tourist visibility in Norway. Havila Kystruten started sailings in 2021 and competes with Hurtigruten on the Bergen to Kirkenes route.

Bangkok-based hospitality group, operating hotels under NH, Anantara, Avani, Tivoli and Oaks, with about 560 hotels in 60 countries. Listed in Bangkok as part of Minor International. Known consumer travel brand, especially in Asia and Europe. Minor Hotels is controlled by Minor International and listed in Thailand; it also includes Avani and Oaks, with strong luxury and mid-market hotel recognition.

Rockville, Maryland-based hotel franchisor, founded 1939, franchising Comfort, Quality, Clarion and Cambria brands, with about 7,500 hotels in 40 countries. Listed on the NYSE (CHH). Known consumer brands in North America. Revenue is franchise royalty fees, earning from hotel owners rather than operating the properties. Well-known US consumer travel brands, with loyalty programme Choice Privileges. Choice franchises about 7,500 hotels and has more than 60 million loyalty members, and it earns royalties rather than owning most properties.

Hong Kong-based luxury hotel group, founded 1971, operating Shangri-La, Kerry and Traders hotels across Asia, listed in Hong Kong. Strong consumer luxury brand in Asia. Operates about 100 hotels in Asia and beyond. Strong luxury brand with high awareness among travellers. Shangri-La Group is based in Hong Kong and listed there; the Kuok family is the controlling shareholder. The group employs tens of thousands of people and is known for its Shangri-La, Kerry and Traders hotel brands, mostly in Asia.

Room00 Group is a Madrid-based hospitality platform, per the input, with funding of about 400 million shown. Scale, hotel brands and customer base are not specified. It appears to operate in the hospitality and accommodation sector in Spain. The input does not list hotel names, number of rooms or investors, so the nature of the group should be verified directly. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Room00 Group is a hospitality platform.

about: Sunstone Hotel Investors is a US real estate investment trust that owns upper-upscale and luxury hotels, typically managed by major brands such as Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt. It owns roughly 15 to 20 hotels in places like Hawaii, California, Florida and Boston, and earns revenue from hotel operations rather than from consumer brands. Based in Aliso Viejo, California, listed on the NYSE (SHO). Owner of hotel real estate, not a hotel brand, so consumer visibility is low; sponsorship fit is mainly hospitality and corporate hospitality.

POOLCORP (Pool Corporation) is the world's largest wholesale distributor of swimming pool supplies, equipment and outdoor living products, operating roughly 450 service centers across North America, Europe and Australia under names such as SCP, Superior Pool Products and Horizon. Customers are pool builders, retailers and service professionals rather than consumers. Based in Covington, Louisiana and listed on Nasdaq (POOL). Annual sales are about 5.5 billion dollars. B2B distributor with limited consumer brand awareness.

Arsenale Group is an Italian multi-brand hospitality and travel group based in Rome, with a portfolio of hotels and resorts, including properties in Italy and other tourist destinations. The Crunchbase description says it provides a multi-brand offer, and funding shown is around 300 million euros. Customers are leisure and business travellers. Brand awareness is mainly regional.

about: Four Seasons Hotel and Residences Jacksonville is a luxury hotel and branded residences development in Jacksonville, Florida, under the Four Seasons brand, announced as part of a large waterfront mixed-use project. Funding shown is about 360 million dollars. Customers are luxury leisure and business travellers and residential buyers. The Four Seasons brand has very high recognition among affluent consumers; this particular property is a local development.

about: NOT A HOTEL is a Tokyo-based Japanese company that develops and sells fractional ownership of design-led villas and hotels, where owners can use their property for part of the year and the rest is operated as a hotel. Properties sit in locations such as Nasu, Hakone, Atami and Hokkaido, as well as overseas projects. Funding of about 47 billion yen is shown. Customers are affluent Japanese buyers. Niche luxury brand, mainly known in Japan.

Prestige Hospitality Ventures is the hospitality arm of Bengaluru's Prestige Group, one of India's largest real estate developers, owning and developing hotels, resorts and serviced apartments. It has partnered with operators such as Hilton, Marriott and others and has hotel assets in Bengaluru and other Indian cities. Funding of about 30 billion rupees is shown. Customers are leisure and business travellers. Parent Prestige has strong regional brand recognition in South India.

Bloomberry Resorts is a Philippine casino resort operator, majority owned by Enrique Razon, that runs Solaire Resort & Casino in Manila's Entertainment City and Solaire North in Quezon City, with hotels, gaming, restaurants and entertainment. Listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (BLOOM). Customers are domestic and regional gamblers and tourists. Strong brand in the Philippines; as a casino operator it is restricted in some sponsorship categories.

American Hotel Income Properties (AHIP) is a Vancouver-based real estate company, TSX-listed (HOT.UN), that owned a portfolio of select-service hotels across the United States under brands such as Marriott, Hilton and IHG franchises, managed by third parties. It ran into debt trouble and sold its assets, with creditors taking control of the portfolio in 2024. B2B hotel owner, not a consumer brand, and no longer a viable sponsor candidate.

DiamondRock Hospitality is a Bethesda, Maryland lodging real estate investment trust, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (DRH), which owns upscale and luxury hotels and resorts in leading US markets and leisure destinations, usually operated by Marriott, Hilton or other management companies. It earns room, food and beverage revenue and pays dividends, owning about 35 hotels. B2B investor-facing, while the hotels trade under well-known brands.

Traveloka is a Southeast Asian online travel and lifestyle platform, founded in Indonesia in 2012 and shown in Crunchbase with a Singapore head office, where users book flights, hotels, trains, attractions and pay bills. It earns commissions and fees and is active in Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines. It has raised about $1.5 billion and has sponsored sport and entertainment in Indonesia. Strong consumer brand across the region.

Trip.com is a leading Chinese online travel agency, founded as Ctrip in 1999 and renamed Trip.com Group, with Crunchbase listing Singapore for its international brand. It sells flights, hotels, trains, packages and tickets through Trip.com, Ctrip, Skyscanner and Qunar, and is listed on Nasdaq (TCOM) and in Hong Kong. Revenue is above 50 billion yuan. It is a strong consumer brand, and a recognised sponsor of sporting events in Europe and Asia.

Stonegate Pub Company is the UK's largest pub operator, based in Shirley, Surrey, with around 4,500 pubs and bars after buying Ei Group in 2020, under brands including Slug and Lettuce, Be At One, Yates and Walkabout. It sells beer, food and drinks to consumers and is owned by TDR Capital. It is highly indebted. Strong consumer visibility, with many pubs showing live sport including Formula 1.

Dalata Hotel Group is Ireland's largest hotel operator, based in Dublin and listed in Dublin and London (DHG), running Maldron and Clayton hotels in Ireland, the UK and continental Europe, with about 50 hotels. It earns room, food and beverage revenue, and has been the subject of takeover interest. Strong local consumer brand in Ireland.

Atour Hotel is a Shanghai-based Chinese mid-to-upscale hotel group, listed on Nasdaq (ATAT), with brands Atour, Atour Light, Zhotel and Ji Hotel, and a retail business selling bedding and lifestyle products. It operates in over a thousand Chinese cities and has several thousand hotels, mostly franchised. Strong domestic consumer brand with younger travellers.

Guesty is a vacation rental management software company with offices in New York and Tel Aviv, and a Crunchbase address in California, which helps property managers handle listings, bookings, payments and guest communication for Airbnb, Booking.com and Vrbo. It has raised about $411 million with a valuation of $2 billion in 2021. B2B, known among short-term rental operators.

Shanghai-based ride-hailing and mobility services company, formed by SAIC Motor, operating a Chinese ride-hailing platform (Cao Cao Mobility is a related brand in the Geely group, not this). Provides one-stop travel services for consumers. Funding figure is CNY 2.6 billion. Backed by the state-owned automaker SAIC. Consumer app in China only; no international profile.

about: Indian real estate developer based in Gurugram, building commercial, retail and residential projects in the Delhi NCR region, including Elan Miracle, Elan Epic and Elan Town Centre malls. Customers are property buyers and corporate tenants. Reported funding is INR 24.9 billion. Private; locally strong brand in the Delhi NCR property market, little consumer profile elsewhere.

London-based luxury hotel group operating Corinthia hotels in London, Budapest, Lisbon, Malta, Prague and Doha, with residences and a spa. Part of Malta's Corinthia group, with Libyan shareholders. Customers are luxury travellers and events clients. Premium brand within the luxury travel segment, with limited mass awareness.

UK holiday park operator with around 30 parks on the British coast, offering caravan and lodge holidays. Part of a larger leisure group. Customers are UK families and holidaymakers. Funding figure is 190 million. Consumer brand with strong UK awareness through TV advertising.

Munich-based holiday rental search engine founded 2014, aggregating millions of holiday homes and apartments from partner platforms for travellers across Europe. Revenue from commissions. Has raised roughly USD 252 million. Consumer travel brand with strong awareness in Germany and moderate across Europe, using heavy online advertising.

Operator of the highway service centres along Ontario's 400-series highways, based in Mississauga, offering fuel, food and retail to travellers at sites featuring brands such as Tim Hortons, Starbucks and Wendy's. Run under a long-term concession from the province and owned by infrastructure investors. Reported funding about USD 250 million. Seen by millions of drivers a year, but low standalone brand awareness.

US amusement park operator based in Sandusky, Ohio, owning parks such as Cedar Point and Knott's Berry Farm. It merged with Six Flags in 2024 to form Six Flags Entertainment Corporation (NYSE). Customers are families and thrill-seekers visiting its parks, and revenue comes from tickets, season passes and food. Strong consumer awareness regionally.

US lodging real estate investment trust based in Orlando, owning upper-upscale hotels and resorts operated by Marriott, Hyatt and Hilton. Listed on the NYSE (XHR). The trust was spun off from InvenTrust Properties in 2015. Revenue comes from hotel operations, with brands such as Marriott and Hyatt paid fees to manage the properties. B2B investor brand with no consumer name.

Amsterdam real estate investment company that, per the input, focuses on hotels, hospitality property management and related property investment. No hotels, funds or scale are listed. It appears to be an investor rather than a hotel brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: US-listed mining company, Critical Metals Corp, developing the Tanbreez rare earths project in Greenland, listed on Nasdaq (CRML). Pre-production resource company with no consumer awareness.

Listed in Hong Kong (0780) as Tongcheng Travel. Crunchbase shows about $1.7 billion in funding. Consumer travel brand in China.

about: Yanolja is a Seoul-based Korean travel platform, with a leading booking app for motels and hotels and a SaaS platform for accommodation operators, expanded through Yanolja Cloud and the acquisition of Interpark. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and GIC. Crunchbase shows about $2 billion in funding. Strong consumer brand in Korea.

Mafengwo is a Beijing based Chinese travel community and booking platform where users share travel guides, reviews and itineraries and book hotels, tours and flights. Founded in 2006, it grew to over 100 million monthly active users at its peak and raised about $500 million from investors including Capital Today and General Atlantic. Revenue comes from travel services and advertising. It planned an IPO that has not taken place. It is a recognized consumer travel brand in China.

Blueground is a New York based provider of furnished apartments for medium- and long-term stays, leasing and managing thousands of units in cities across the US, Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Customers include relocating professionals and corporate clients, who rent via an app. Founded in 2013 in Greece, it has raised about $303 million. It is a hospitality-style consumer brand with moderate awareness among business travelers and expats.

TerraPay is a London based global payments company providing cross-border payments and remittances into wallets, bank accounts and cash points across dozens of markets, working with mobile operators, banks and fintechs. Founded in 2014 by Ambar Chandra and Ambarish Kenghe among others, it has licences in several jurisdictions and has raised about $259 million. It is a B2B payments infrastructure brand, with limited consumer awareness but a strong position in remittances from the Gulf, Asia and Africa.

Vinpearl is the Vietnamese hotel, resort and leisure brand of Vingroup, operating luxury hotels, resorts, golf courses, theme parks and the VinWonders and Vinpearl Safari attractions, with properties in Nha Trang, Phu Quoc, Da Nang and other destinations. It sits within the Vingroup conglomerate founded by Pham Nhat Vuong, with its parent Vinpearl JSC. It is a major domestic tourism and hospitality consumer brand in Vietnam. Funding is shown at about $255 million.

Auro Travel (Auro New Transport Concept) is a Madrid based Spanish company described as the largest VTC (ride-hailing with driver) operator in Spain, offering chauffeur-driven transport. Crunchbase records about 230 million euros of funding. The input is limited on ownership and fleet size. It is a consumer transport service business with regional brand recognition in Spain. It has grown by acquiring local management firms. Funding shown is about $220 million, probably private equity backed. Guests book via its website and online travel platforms. It is a consumer-facing hospitality brand with regional awareness.

about: Oberoi Realty is a Mumbai based Indian real estate developer building premium residential, commercial, retail and hospitality projects, mainly in Mumbai, such as Oberoi Garden City in Goregaon, Three Sixty West and Commerz towers, and it owns a stake in the Oberoi hotel at Worli and a mall. Founded in 1980 by Vikas Oberoi, it is listed on the NSE and BSE (OBEROIRLTY). Customers are homebuyers and corporate tenants. It is a high-end property brand in Mumbai with limited awareness elsewhere.

AvantStay is an Austin, Texas luxury vacation rental company that operates large, professionally managed homes in destinations such as Lake Tahoe, Scottsdale, Palm Springs, Nashville and Miami, with design, concierge and cleaning services. Founded in 2016, it is a tech-enabled hospitality brand booked by groups and families through its site and app. It raised about $186 million in funding, including a Series B in 2021 and debt. It is a consumer brand with a modest profile in the US.

Exoticca is a Barcelona based online travel company selling packaged tours and trips to destinations across Asia, Africa, Latin America and Europe, with flights, hotels and guides included. Customers book through its website and app in Spain, the UK, the US, Italy and Latin America. Founded in 2016, it has raised around 175 million euros, including funding from Sofina and others. It is a consumer travel brand advertised on TV and online in Spain and other markets.

h.wood Group is a Los Angeles hospitality and lifestyle company operating restaurants, nightclubs and lounges such as Delilah, Bootsy Bellows, Poppy, Nobu Malibu, Craig's and The Nice Guy, with locations in Los Angeles, Las Vegas, Miami, New York and London. It is a private company that serves a celebrity and affluent clientele and also runs events. Founded by John Terzian in 2008, its Crunchbase funding is about $189 million. It is a consumer hospitality brand with a strong celebrity profile.

about: Hurb (formerly Hotel Urbano) is a Rio de Janeiro based Brazilian online travel agency selling hotel stays, packages, flights and experiences at discounted prices, mostly to domestic Brazilian customers. Founded in 2011, it had investors such as Qatar Investment Authority and others, with total funding of about $193 million. It is a widely advertised consumer travel brand in Brazil and has been a sponsor of Brazilian football clubs.

Wander is an Austin, Texas luxury vacation rental company that operates high-end homes with smart-home technology, curated amenities and concierge services in destinations such as Joshua Tree, Big Sur and Lake Tahoe. Founded in 2019 by Dylan Rice and Ryan Wang, it has expanded across the US and abroad and has raised about $198 million. Guests book through its website and app. It is a consumer travel brand, known mostly among affluent US travelers.

Kasa Living is a New York based hospitality company operating apartment-hotels, with a tech-enabled model that turns apartment buildings, and hotel rooms, into short- and long-stay lodging with contactless check-in and an app. Founded in 2016, it has properties across US cities and acquired Stay Alfred in 2022. It has raised about $166 million from investors including Sorenson Capital and others. It is a consumer travel brand with moderate awareness.

Limehome is a Munich based provider of digital aparthotels, converting vacant commercial spaces into serviced apartments with self check-in via an app, with locations across Germany, Austria, the UK, France, Spain and other European countries. Founded in 2016 by Lukas Pieczonka and Lars Henrik Wagner, it has raised around 156 million euros from investors including Eurazeo and Ralph Winter. It is a consumer travel brand known mostly in Germany and among business travelers.

Grande Asset Hotels and Property is a Thai hotel owner and operator based in Bangkok, controlling the Royal Orchid Hotel and Grande Centre Point brands and properties in Thailand. It is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (GRAND) and part of the Grande group. Hospitality brand with local consumer awareness in Thailand.

Royal Orchid Hotel is the hotel company behind the Royal Orchid Sheraton Hotel in Bangkok, based on the Chao Phraya river in Bang Rak. It is owned by Grande Asset Hotels and Property and owns and operates hotel assets in Thailand. Hospitality business with local awareness in Thailand.

Korean Air is South Korea's flag carrier, based in Seoul, flying passengers and cargo to about 100 cities worldwide from its Incheon hub, and is part of the SkyTeam alliance. In 2024 it completed its acquisition of Asiana Airlines. It also makes aerospace components, and is the core company of the Hanjin group. Listed on the Korea Exchange (003490). Strong consumer brand and a long-standing sponsor of sport and cultural events.

Alandalus Property Company is a Saudi real estate firm based in Riyadh that owns and operates commercial properties, including Andalus Mall in Jeddah, plus hotels and hospitality assets. It is listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul). Consumer-facing through its malls in Saudi Arabia, with moderate local awareness.

SALTO Systems is a Spanish maker of electronic access control and smart locks, based in Oiartzun, Gipuzkoa, serving hotels, offices, universities, hospitals and residential buildings with cloud-based and wireless door locking systems. Founded in 2001, it sells in many countries through partners. Privately held. B2B brand known among hoteliers and integrators, not consumers.

YY Group Holding is a Singapore-based live streaming agency and hospitality-freelance services company, working with hosts and talent on platforms such as BIGO Live in Asia, and also offering freelance staffing. Listed on Nasdaq (YYGH) since 2024. B2B and creator economy business with small public brand awareness.

Club Med is a French all-inclusive holiday resort operator founded in 1950 by Gerard Blitz, known for beach and ski resorts around the world with sports, kids' clubs and dining included. It runs about 65-70 villages in dozens of countries and sells to families and couples, mostly European and Asian guests. Headquartered in Paris, it has been owned by Chinese conglomerate Fosun International since 2015 after being delisted from Euronext. Revenue is about 2 billion euros. Very well known consumer travel brand, particularly in France and China.
